title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff + regional failover (prevent thrashing)
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Hotfix: prevent SLO enforcer thrashing during regional circuit-breaker storms by tightening backoff/jitter, isolating region counters, and adding cooldowns. Improves stability of regional failover and reduces unnecessary global load-shedding.
description:
Background: In production incident SUP-887 we observed the SLO enforcer entering a rapid failover loop when multiple regions reported transient capacity pressure. Root cause: the backoff implementation in slo-enforcer used a global retry cadence and a shared token bucket that caused regions to influence each other; combined with small jitter values this produced thrashing and aggressive global load-shedding.

This PR introduces a targeted hotfix to stabilize behavior: 1) Per-region backoff state and counters so transient issues in one region don't immediately trigger global failover; 2) Increased base backoff and adaptive exponential backoff with capped jitter to avoid synchronized retries; 3) A cooldown window applied after a circuit-breaker trip to avoid immediate re-evaluation; 4) Additional observability (region-tagged metrics and a debug log when cooldowns are active); 5) Unit and integration tests that reproduce the thrash pattern and validate the cooldown/backoff behavior.

Checklist:
- [x] Isolate region-level state and counters
- [x] Implement adaptive exponential backoff + bounded jitter
- [x] Add cooldown window for circuit-breaker recovery
- [x] Add metrics & logs (slo_enforcer.backoff_ms, slo_enforcer.cooldown_active, region tag)
- [x] Unit tests and integration canary test
- [x] CI green and canary validated in perf-lab

Notes: This is intentionally conservative (stronger backoff + explicit cooldown) to restore stability quickly. Follow-up work will evaluate tuning and dynamic policies (ENG-4237).
